title: The rate model's maximum-profit utilization is set at 70%, below the 90% utilization it targets
content:
The `Rfactor` deduction in the stUSDS Rate is defined in A.4.4.1.3.2.1.5 as a closed-form expression in `u_m`, `u_opt`, `alpha`, `beta` and `slope1`. Two of its inputs are named in a way that reveals intent: A.4.4.1.3.2.1.5.1 calls `u_m` "the maximum profit utilization" (currently 70%, A.4.4.1.3.2.1.5.1.1), and A.4.4.1.3.2.1.5.4 describes `beta` as "a tuning parameter that determines how much profit is made at maximum utilization" (currently 100%).

The notable fact is the gap. The rate-setting mechanism steers utilization toward `u_opt` = 90% (A.4.4.1.3.5.1), while the profit calibration is centred on 70%. The operating point the system pushes toward is therefore *not* the point at which the retained spread is greatest.

That separation is worth naming explicitly because it is unusual. A protocol that tuned both to the same utilization would be maximizing its own take at equilibrium; splitting them means the target is chosen for capital efficiency and market clearing, while the profit curve peaks earlier — so at the target, the deduction is past its most favourable point and lender yield has more of the spread.

Having `beta` as a separate dial for "how much profit is made at maximum utilization" also makes the extraction level an explicit, auditable parameter rather than an emergent side-effect of the curve. Anyone assessing whether stUSDS is priced fairly should read `u_m` and `beta` as the protocol's take-rate settings, and note that they can be moved without touching the visible borrow-rate curve at all.
description: Rfactor is calibrated around u_m = 70% while the borrow rate targets 90%, so the system does not steer toward the point where its own take is greatest.
